title: Measure real network throughput on Linux, macOS and Windows; unblock System Monitor without requiring a page switch.
changes: Read monotonic RX/TX byte counters from active Linux /proc/net/dev adapters, bounded macOS /usr/sbin/netstat -ibn link rows and Windows Get-NetAdapterStatistics; discard duplicate, inactive and unsafe interface records.
Compute real per-second rates from two device-side samples even on cold start, coalesce concurrent probes, preserve genuine 0 B/s, and never convert unavailable counters into fabricated values.

Normalize bounded Windows adapter aliases (including spaces), preserve existing owner-scoped diagnostics API contracts and show measured rates in the device header, System Monitor summary and per-interface panels.
Start the first live scan independently of archive history while avoiding StrictMode duplicate requests; resume missing network measurements from sibling tabs even with numeric-only archived history.
Use skeletons only while scans are pending, then show actual readings or explicit unavailable/retry states; never leave the lower System Monitor visually empty after history loading.

Verify Linux device-side rates, Windows parser/backend regressions and desktop/mobile Playwright scenarios with delayed history. A physical Windows runtime smoke remains required before release approval.
